Write an email to a colleague about a new hobby you have taken up. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: A new hobby, and a confession

Hi Marcus,

You asked last week what I had been doing with my Saturdays, and I gave you a vague answer. The truth is that I have taken up bread baking, and I am a good deal more interested in it than I expected to be.

It started in August, when my sister sent me a jar of her sourdough starter. She is a very persuasive woman, so it came with instructions, a warning that it must be fed every day, and a note saying she would know if I let it die. I named the thing Gerald and put him on the kitchen counter. For the first week he did nothing at all but sit there and smell faintly of old socks. Then one morning he had doubled in size and was bubbling away like he had somewhere to be.

My first loaf was a failure. It came out of the oven flat as a dinner plate and hard enough that Priya said we might use it to prop open the back door. The second was better, but the crust was pale and sorry looking. By the fourth I had learned that the trouble was mostly patience. You cannot hurry bread. It wants to rest and rise in its own time, and if you push it, it lets you know. I have never been much good at waiting, so this has been a humbling sort of lesson.

Now I get up early on Saturdays, mix the dough, and then wander around the house doing small chores while it works. I fold it every half hour, and I check it more often than I need to. The best part comes at the end, when the loaf is out of the oven and cooling on the rack and you can hear the crust crackle as it settles. Priya says it is the only time I am ever quiet.

Last weekend I brought two loaves to my neighbor, an older gentleman who lives alone, and he came to the door the next day with a jar of plum jam. I think that is the real reason I like it. Bread seems to start conversations that otherwise would never happen.

If you would like to try some, I will bring a loaf on Monday. Fair warning, though: if it turns out flat, you are not to say anything. I will also gladly part with a little of Gerald, should you want to start your own.

All the best,
[name]
